lines.text: She called him *at 2am.*
On her anniversary.
Her husband had forgotten. *Again.*
He ate the pepper soup, watched the match, and at ten he kissed the air near her temple and went to bed.
The dress was still on.
*Wine-red.* Cut low at the back. Bought in Lagos and hidden for six months, waiting for tonight.
Seven years married.
She couldn’t remember the last time a man’s eyes stayed on her long enough *to undress her.*
At 1:58, her thumb found his name.
*Chris.*
The boy from university who walked her to the hostel every night and never once tried to come inside.
She had waited, every night, *for him to try.*
One ring. Two.
*“Lily.”*
Low and unhurried, as if he had been holding her name in his mouth for eight years.
*“What colour is the dress?”*
Something warm unfolded low in her stomach.
He breathed out slowly, as if the word had touched him.
*“Are you still wearing it?”*
“Yes.”
*“Then go where he can’t hear you.”*
She slipped into the parlour. The tiles were cold under her bare feet.
*Her skin was not.*
*“Find the zip,”* he said.
Her fingers found it at the small of her back.
*“Slowly, Lily. I want to hear it.”*
The zip whispered down. The dress loosened at her shoulders.
One strap slipped. *Then the other.*
Her breath caught, and he heard that too.
*“Close your eyes,”* he whispered. *“And let your hand go where mine would.”*
*She did.*
Then NEPA brought the light back.
Every bulb in the flat blazed on at once.
Behind her, the bedroom door stood open.
*She had closed it.*
